chunks: From him, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Whoever intends an evil deed, then let him not do it, for perhaps the servant commits the evil deed, and the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, sees him, then says: “By My honour and My majesty, I shall never forgive you after that.”

key_terms.الرَّبُّ: the Lord, meaning Allah, Blessed and Exalted
key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: the servant, meaning the human being before Allah
key_terms.بِسَيِّئَةٍ: an evil deed or sinful act
key_terms.هَمَّ: intended or resolved to do something
key_terms.وَعِزَّتِي وَجَلَالِي: an oath by divine honour and majesty

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach about intending and committing a sinful deed?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against carrying out sinful intentions, urging a person to abandon an evil deed before committing it. It emphasizes the gravity of sin before Allah, the Exalted, and serves as a strong moral deterrent by reminding the believer of divine judgment and the possible loss of forgiveness.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who thinks of an evil deed, so he should not do it, for perhaps the servant does the evil deed, and the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Sees him and He<sup>azwj</sup> would be Saying: “By My<sup>azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup>azwj</sup> Majesty, I<sup>azwj</sup> will not Forgive you after that, ever!”’.
en.sarwar: 17. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

One who thinks to commit a sin, must not commit it; perhaps a servant (of Allah) commits a sin and the Lord, the Most Blessed, the Most High, finds him in that condition. He will say, ‘I swear by my Majesty and Glory that I will never forgive you thereafter.’”
